paras: The attempted lynching of John Revel happened at Twenty-eighth Street and Eighth Avenue in New York City early on a Saturday in December 1903, when a crowd tried to take Revel, described as 'a young negro', from police officers and hang him to a lamp-post. The police drew their revolvers and the crowd gave way, and Revel was taken off by his captors. The episode ran as a wire item under the headline 'Attempt to Lynch Negro in New York' and was notable as a lynching attempt in a Northern city.

According to the New York dispatch, Revel had just shot Katherine Miller, 'an old woman of his race', probably fatally, and had also hit Agnes Brennan, who was described as an 'innocent spectator'. The shootings are reported only as accusations, and the dispatch gives no cause for them.

As police held Revel at the corner, the crowd took up the cry 'Lynch him! Lynch him!' and closed in on him. One man, whom the dispatch called a 'wildeyed fellow' with 'all the elements of a riotmaker', shouted to hang Revel from a lamp-post, and others repeated the call. The officers then drew their pistols and aimed them at the leaders pressing in on them, and most of the crowd fell back. About half a dozen men held their ground until they were told they would be shot if they did not clear a way for Revel and the police.
The coverage found does not report what became of Revel, whether Katherine Miller died, or whether anyone in the crowd was arrested.

The only report found is a New York dispatch dated December 14 that the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic of Arkansas printed on its front page that day. The dispatch put Revel's race in the headline and treated his guilt as settled, calling him 'the would-be murderer', while casting the man who led the call for a hanging as a 'riotmaker' and crediting the police with stopping the crowd. No account in the Black press was found.

bases: A crowd cried 'Lynch him!' and tried to take Revel from the police to hang him to a lamp-post, but officers held it off, so this was an attempted lynching (A1).
A crowd, with 'half a dozen bolder spirits' at its front, tried to seize Revel from police to hang him for a shooting he was accused of, but no one was killed (A1).
A single New York dispatch, printed in the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic, is the only report found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: New York wire dispatch
accounts.gist: A crowd tried to seize Revel from the police and hang him to a lamp-post after he was accused of shooting two women. Police drew revolvers, and the crowd gave way.

framing.detail: An Arkansas paper ran the New York dispatch on its front page under 'ATTEMPT TO LYNCH NEGRO IN NEW YORK'. The dispatch treats Revel's guilt as established ('the would-be murderer') and describes the man who led the call to hang him as having 'all the elements of a riotmaker'.

record_check.dossier: Supported as an inference only: the dispatch, dated Monday, December 14, says 'early Saturday', which makes the date December 12 by the calendar
Accused of shooting Katherine Miller (probably fatally) and Agnes Brennan, a bystander
An attempted seizure and threats to hang him; the crowd never got Revel away from the police
Supported: Revel was held by police throughout and was not taken from them

info: Early Saturday morning before a dispatch dated Monday, December 14, 1903; by the calendar this was Saturday, December 12, 1903 (the date is not printed)
Corner of Twenty-eighth street and Eighth avenue, New York
John Revel, described as 'a young negro', the target of the crowd
Accused of shooting Katherine Miller, 'an old woman of his race', probably fatally, and Agnes Brennan, a bystander
An 'angry crowd', not named and of unstated race; one 'wildeyed fellow' urged the hanging
None reported killed by the crowd; Katherine Miller, described as Black, was reported 'probably fatally' shot by Revel
The crowd fell back and the police took Revel away; he was not lynched

sources.note: New York dispatch dated Dec. 14: a crowd tried to take John Revel, 'a young negro', from police at Twenty-eighth street and Eighth avenue to hang him; police drew pistols. The only report found.
quotes: An angry crowd tried to take John Revel, a young negro, from the police early Saturday, at the corner of Twenty-eighth street and Eighth avenue, and hang him to a lamp-post.
He had shot Katherine Miller, an old woman of his race, probably fatally, and Agnes Brennan, who had been an innocent spectator of his attempt.
the police drew their pistols and leveled them at the leaders of the crowd, who were pressing in on them.
they did not break ground until they were told they would be shot if they did not open a way for Revel and his captors.
